Cable Internet lets your phone use your computer\'s internet through a USB cable: fast, stable, and without Wi‑Fi or mobile data.
The phone creates a local VPN interface and forwards its traffic through the USB cable (adb reverse) to a small relay program on your computer, which reaches the internet for it.

Cable Internet collects nothing. It does not record, store or send your data, browsing or location. Your traffic only travels through the USB cable to your own computer. There are no ads, no analytics and no account.
Uses the Gnirehtet relay protocol by Genymobile (Apache License 2.0) and Android Platform Tools (Apache License 2.0).
Use your computer\'s internet on your phone over USB with Cable Internet: %1$s

string-array.name: g_pc
string-array.item: Install and open the Cable Internet program on your Windows computer.
Plug your phone in with a USB cable that carries data (not a charge-only cable).
Wait until the program says the phone is ready.

string-array.name: g_generic
string-array.item: Open Settings and go to About phone.
Tap Build number 7 times in a row. Enter your lock-screen PIN if asked.
Go back to Settings and open Developer options (often under System or Additional settings).
Turn on USB debugging and confirm.
Connect the phone to the computer with the cable.
On the phone, tick Always allow on the Allow USB debugging? prompt and tap Allow.

string-array.name: g_samsung
string-array.item: Settings → About phone → Software information.
Tap Build number 7 times and enter your PIN.
Go back: Developer options now appears at the bottom of Settings.
Turn on USB debugging.
Plug in the cable and tap Allow (tick Always allow).
If the prompt never appears: Settings → Security and privacy → Auto Blocker → turn it off (or turn off Block commands via USB cable).

string-array.name: g_xiaomi
string-array.item: Settings → About phone.
Tap MIUI version (or OS version on HyperOS) 7 times.
Settings → Additional settings → Developer options.
Turn on USB debugging, Install via USB and USB debugging (Security settings) — whichever you have.
Plug in the cable and tap Allow. Without Install via USB, installing the app from the PC is blocked.

string-array.name: g_huawei
string-array.item: Settings → About phone.
Tap Build number 7 times.
Settings → System & updates → Developer options.
Turn on USB debugging (and Allow ADB debugging in charge only mode, if shown).
Plug in the cable, choose Transfer files as the USB mode and tap Allow.

string-array.name: g_oppo
string-array.item: Settings → About device → Version.
Tap Build number 7 times.
Settings → Additional settings → Developer options.
Turn on USB debugging.
Plug in the cable and tap Allow. If installing the app is refused, also turn on Install via USB or Disable permission monitoring.

string-array.name: g_vivo
string-array.item: Settings → More settings (or System) → About phone.
Tap Software version or Build number 7 times.
Go back and open Developer options.
Turn on USB debugging.
Plug in the cable and tap Allow.

string-array.name: g_trouble
string-array.item: Cable: some cables only charge. Use the original cable.
Port: plug straight into the computer, not into a hub.
Screen: keep the phone unlocked and awake.
USB mode: pull down the notification shade and choose File transfer (MTP).
No Allow prompt: in Developer options tap Revoke USB debugging authorizations, switch USB debugging off and on, then replug the cable.
Driver: run Windows Update, or install your brand\'s phone program (for example Samsung Smart Switch) once to get its driver.
Other programs that use adb (Mi PC Suite, HiSuite, Android Studio) can block the connection. Close them, or restart the phone and computer.
